articles.title: House Republicans Block Hegseth Impeachment, but Democrats Could Revive Effort in January
articles.summary: The Republican-led House on Tuesday narrowly rejected a push to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth over unauthorized military hostilities in Iran, Venezuela and Yemen, shielding one of President Donald Trump's closest allies from an immediate reckoning but setting the stage for a renewed confrontation when Democrats take control of Congress in January. articles.title: How Israel Will Choose Its Next Prime Minister, Explained
articles.summary: Israeli President Isaac Herzog on Sunday tasked Gadi Eisenkot , a former military chief and the leader of the center-right Yashar party, with forming the country’s next government. It’s the first of several steps necessary to determine the next Prime Minister—but a potentially months-long process could leave Benjamin Netanyahu in power for the foreseeable future. articles.title: Hegseth Could Still Be the Third Cabinet Secretary to be Impeached. What Happened to the Others?
articles.summary: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth narrowly escaped an impeachment attempt Tuesday after the Republican-led House rejected a resolution filed by a GOP lawmaker. While Hegseth has been granted a reprieve, it's possible the Democrats could revive the effort in January, when they take control of both the House and Senate following sweeping victories in the midterms. articles.title: Trump Says 'You Should've Had Stock' to Build Net Worth. Here's How He's Increased His by Billions in His Second Term
articles.summary: In the two years since President Donald Trump was re-elected to the White House, his reported net worth has spiked by billions of dollars. Between 2024—during his presidential campaign—and 2025, Trump’s net worth rose from $4.3 billion to $7.3 billion, according to a Forbes report published in September 2025.
